A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distribution-calibrated BTD aggregation study. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–I are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original WMT and Reward Bench 2 experiments, comparisons with human raters, and calibration, temperature, positional-bias and prompt-variation analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, and adds confidence intervals to the prompt/model tie-rate comparison.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same count features, Davidson probabilities, DRPS fitting objective and MAE Bayes decision rule. Removing the introduction's maximum-likelihood wording corrects an inconsistency: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 already specify DRPS in v1. The extensions in Section 6 remain future work.

E1.justification: Both evaluate WMT23 English–German and Chinese–English, the same six Reward Bench 2 tasks, and the same transfer, prompt-variation and positional-order scenarios. No new dataset or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SC, Soft-SC, CI-SC, USC and generative self-aggregation, with GD and FS also retained in Figure 2. The newly cited AtC method is discussed only as related work, not evaluated.

E3.justification: The 5% calibration split, evaluation remainder, MAE and pairwise-accuracy metrics, judge models, sampling budgets, temperature settings and order balancing are retained. Using N for evaluation-set size and rho for the calibration ratio clarifies notation without changing the protocol.

E4.justification: The transfer, calibration-size, confusion-matrix, fitted-parameter, positional-order, temperature and prompt-variation analyses already appear in v1. V2 relocates displays and adds explanatory cross-references, including to the existing n=20 results in Table 11.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports 95% confidence intervals for individual tie rates and their averages, described as quantifying data-sampling variance. Existing split counts, permutation testing, Figure 2 confidence intervals and appendix uncertainty summaries remain unchanged; additional experimental runs are not established.

E6.justification: Section 3 newly reports an explicit statistical-significance finding from the non-overlapping intervals around Gemini's 12.4% and 37.6% prompt-dependent tie rates. Table 2's point estimates, the benchmark scores in Tables 3–7, and all appendix result entries and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12, the expected-risk expressions and the DRPS consistency and optimization arguments are mathematically unchanged. Revised symbols and equation formatting do not add definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: calibrated aggregation improves MAE and pairwise accuracy over standard aggregation and can match or exceed individual raters against human-consensus labels. Neither the central contribution nor its demonstrated scope changes.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds a specific explanation for Factuality-to-Precise IF transfer failure: an extreme calibration correction forces excessive tie predictions. V1 discussed mismatched calibration regimes more generally. Section 6 also elaborates prospective ordinal, multidimensional and heterogeneous-judge extensions.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes v1's statement that L-BFGS-B uses 'few random restarts,' reducing optimizer documentation without establishing that the implementation changed. The smoothing constants, appendix box constraints, data construction and substantive prompt instructions remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds AtC (Xie et al., 2026), distinguishing its isotonic calibration of continuous scores to human consensus from direct calibration of ternary judgments. Most other reference edits update bibliographic metadata or consolidate the duplicate Gemini reference.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the introduction and experimental-setup explanation, clarifies notation, separates offline and online algorithm steps, and expands future work. It also adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. Figures 11–15 move after Appendix I; Table 2 gains interval annotations, and Figures 1–2 gain explanatory captions. All existing figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful uncertainty reporting in Table 2 and removes the introduction's maximum-likelihood description that conflicted with the unchanged DRPS procedure. Clearer notation, captions and related-work positioning provide further limited gains. The empirical evidence is otherwise unchanged, and losing the optimizer-restart detail slightly reduces reproducibility, so the net improvement is modest.
